name: GitHub Actions CI
description: GitHub Actions — reusable workflows, matrix strategies, caching, secrets handling, environment protection
content:
# GitHub Actions CI Best Practices

- Use reusable workflows (`workflow_call`) for shared CI logic across repositories — avoid duplicating workflow definitions
- Use matrix strategies to test across multiple OS, language, and dependency versions — fail fast with `fail-fast: true` for quicker feedback
- Cache dependencies (`actions/cache` or built-in caching in setup actions) to speed up builds — cache `node_modules`, pip, Go modules, etc.
- Never hardcode secrets in workflow files — use GitHub Secrets and reference them as `${{ secrets.NAME }}`, and use `${{ vars.NAME }}` for non-sensitive configuration
- Use environment protection rules for production deployments — require approvals and limit which branches can deploy
- Pin action versions to full commit SHAs (not tags) for security — e.g., `actions/checkout@abcdef123` instead of `actions/checkout@v4`
- Use `concurrency` groups to cancel redundant runs — prevent multiple deployments or test runs from overlapping on the same branch
- Keep jobs granular and independent — use `needs` for dependencies, but allow unrelated jobs to run in parallel
- Use `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions at the job level with least privilege — set `permissions:` explicitly rather than using defaults
- Add status checks and branch protection rules — require CI to pass before merging to main
